title: The said-back prediction moment builds only on a plain yes: a long yes no longer loops, and a yes naming another moment never builds the old one
request: The owner, in a cloud session: review the repository after 37.11 (the lead agent as Home's default) and track the approved plan (build path, route, speed, final test, cost).
spec: Step 0 of the plan says the build path must work end to end with no trade allowed, and the moment is the prediction contract (rule 1). When Home says the moment back: a plain yes of any length builds; a yes naming another time says the new moment back; other words get the question again or go to the agent; a hold builds nothing.
plan: Read the 37.11 diff against the plan's step 0
Probe the confirm-moment step with natural answers outside the tests
Write failing tests for the answers that loop
Narrow the correction words, add the hold, keep the said-back correction
Run the affected tests, record, rebuild the dev SFT set
Send the diff to the dclab-reviewer; rework on its findings with a whitelist of approval words

decisions.decision: Build only when every word of the answer is plain approval (a whitelist) and a yes word is present
decisions.why: a blacklist of correction words cannot see every correction; with the moment as the prediction contract, an unknown word must block the build, not allow it

decisions.decision: Leftover words naming a time are said back as the new moment, after stripping a leading yes/no/not quite/wait/actually/but
decisions.why: "Yes, it is at checkout, not at signup" is a correction, and the person confirms the new moment before anything is built

decisions.decision: A yes with other leftover words is asked again with the old moment kept; no yes and no time goes to the agent
decisions.why: saying back words that are not a moment stored garbage as the contract on the next yes; a change of subject must reach the agent

decisions.decision: A hold on the build (hold off/on, not yet ... build, build ... later) drops the question

change: dclab_rnd/draft/case_home.py (CORRECTION replaced by HOLD_BUILD, APPROVAL, YES_WORD, TIME_WORDS, LEADING_ANSWER and _say_moment_back; the confirm-moment branch); tests/test_case_home.py (six tests)

findings.defect: A long yes to the said-back moment was taken as a new moment
findings.scenario: Home: "So the prediction is made at checkout ... Shall I build with that?" Person: "Yes, that is correct, go ahead". Home: "So the prediction is made that is correct, go ahead, using only what is known then. Shall I build with that?" and again on every full-sentence yes
findings.cause: the confirm step treated any yes longer than four words as a correction, stripped the leading yes and said the rest back as the moment; a bare "no" or "not" anywhere also counted as a correction
findings.fix: a correction only on but/instead/rather/actually or a leading no; a hold builds nothing; any other yes builds

findings.defect: The first fix built any yes, so a yes naming another moment built the old one silently
findings.scenario: Home says back "at signup"; the person: "Yes, it is at checkout, not at signup" (or "Sure, it should be at checkout after payment"); the project is built with the prediction made at signup, a wrong prediction contract
findings.cause: the fix narrowed the correction words to but/instead/rather/actually and a leading no, and any message starting with yes passed says_yes, so every other correction became a build
findings.fix: build only on a whitelist of approval words; leftover words naming a time are said back as the new moment

findings.defect: A "but" or leading "no" that is not a correction was said back as the moment
findings.scenario: "No problem, go ahead" said back as "problem, go ahead"; "Not quite, it's at checkout" as "quite, it's at checkout"; a second yes would store that text as the prediction moment
findings.cause: any but or leading no counted as a correction and the rest was said back whatever it was
findings.fix: plain approval ("no problem", "nothing else to add") builds; only words naming a time are said back, after stripping not quite/wait/actually; other words are asked again

findings.scenario: "Yes that's right, but I'll build later" was said back as a moment
findings.cause: HOLD_BUILD matched only a delay word before build
findings.fix: HOLD_BUILD also matches build/start followed by later/yet/tomorrow/next week, and hold on

outcome: The build path's last step builds only on a plain yes: a long yes builds, a yes naming another moment is said back, other words are asked again or go to the agent. Not measured live: the 37.11 live check never reached the build's moment question.
lessons: A rule that reads a person's words needs probing with natural answers, not only the ones its tests were written from
Length is a weak signal for meaning: a long yes is still a yes
When a misread is costly (here the prediction contract), whitelist what may act and let everything else ask again; a blacklist of corrections fails open
Fixing a loop by accepting more is a trade: check what the wider acceptance now lets through before pushing
risks: The moment question still takes any non-question of three or more words as the moment; the said-back step keeps it safe, but it reads oddly
The time words are a heuristic: a correction naming no time word ("Yes, the plan is checkout") is asked again rather than said back
The first fix was pushed before its review; it built a yes naming another moment for one commit on the session branch only (no live use)
